0.title: Getting started
0.content: Use this site to learn the documentation flow and check a change before adopting the workflows in a product repository.

1.title: Table of contents
1.content: . | How the site is published | Propose a documentation change | Write a sample help page | Check the result | .

2.title: How the site is published
2.content: The documentation lives on the gh-pages branch of DiRoots.Sandbox.Releases. GitHub Pages reads that branch and uses Jekyll to turn the Markdown pages into a website. The develop branch is the repository’s default branch. It will hold the trusted publishing caller when the preview workflows are installed. The website’s files and the preview build caller belong in the documentation branch.

3.title: Propose a documentation change
3.content: . | Start a new branch from gh-pages. | Edit a sample page, such as the sample sentence on the homepage. | Open a pull request targeting gh-pages. | Review the text and formatting before merging it. | . When the PR merges, GitHub Pages rebuilds the sandbox website. A temporary PR preview is a separate feature that will become available after the shared workflows are connected.

4.title: Write a sample help page
4.content: A documentation page starts with settings between two lines of three dashes. These settings tell the theme which layout, sidebar title and position to use. --- layout: default title: Example help page nav_order: 5 --- # Example help page Explain one task in a short paragraph. 1. Describe the first step. 2. Describe the expected result.

5.title: Check the result
5.content: Use the sidebar to switch pages, try the search box and follow an internal link. The preview checklist lists the checks to repeat when automatic previews are enabled.

6.title: DiRoots Documentation Sandbox
6.content: A place to test documentation previews before using them in DiRoots product manuals. This site contains sample documentation. It uses the same Just the Docs theme as the DiStem manual, with a sidebar, page search and links between help pages. Used for testing workflows.

7.title: What this sandbox is for
7.content: The sandbox lets us change a page, review how it looks and test the shared workflows in DiRoots.Public.Workflows. It represents the documentation part of a product’s .Releases repository. The first setup adds these pages and publishes the sandbox website. Automatic previews of pull requests are now connected: this sentence only appears in the PR preview until the pull request is merged.

12.title: Before previews are enabled
12.content: Check the published sandbox site after this initial setup merges: . | The homepage and all three help pages load. | The sidebar highlights the current page. | Search finds the phrase sandbox example from the homepage. | Internal links stay inside the sandbox website. | The pages remain readable in a narrow browser window. | .

13.title: Open and update a preview
13.content: . | Create a branch from gh-pages and change the homepage’s sample sentence. | Open a pull request targeting gh-pages. | Wait for the build and publication workflows to succeed. | Open the preview link posted by the workflow on the PR. | Confirm the preview contains the changed sentence while the main sandbox site still shows the merged version. | Push another edit to the same branch and confirm the preview and its existing comment update. | . These preview steps require the workflows and GitHub App access to be configured first.

14.title: Expected lifecycle
14.content: | Action | Expected result after previews are enabled | . | Open a same-repository documentation PR | A temporary website and one preview comment appear. | . | Update the PR | The preview shows the latest eligible build. | . | Close the PR without merging | The preview is removed; the main site keeps its existing content. | . | Merge the PR | The main site receives the changes and the temporary preview is removed. | . | Introduce a build error | The workflow reports a failure and does not publish a new preview. | .

15.title: Check formatting
15.content: This page includes headings, an ordered list, a bullet list and a table so reviewers can compare their appearance in the published site and a preview. Return to Getting started or the homepage.

16.title: Terms explained
16.content: A few terms used when working on the documentation website. | Term | Meaning in this sandbox | . | Markdown | Plain text with simple formatting for headings, links, lists and tables. The help pages are Markdown files. | . | Jekyll | The tool that turns the source pages and settings into a website. | . | Just the Docs | The theme that provides the sidebar, search and page styling, also used by DiStem’s documentation. | . | GitHub Pages | The GitHub service that builds and hosts the sandbox website. | . | gh-pages | The branch containing this site’s documentation. It is a branch name rather than a separate service. | . | Pull request or PR | A proposed change that can be reviewed before it is merged into a branch. | . | Documentation preview | A temporary version of the website showing a PR’s proposed changes. | . | Workflow | Automated instructions that build, publish, update or remove a site. | . | GitHub App | The integration that will give the publishing workflow permission to write preview files. | .

17.title: Website and preview
17.content: The main sandbox website shows the documentation merged into gh-pages. Once previews are enabled, a PR preview will show proposed changes before they are merged. Closing a PR will remove its temporary preview. Start with Getting started to try a documentation change.
